explanation: Binary-search the largest integer whose square does not exceed k. Use 64-bit multiplication so squaring a 32-bit candidate cannot overflow.
timeComplexity: O(log(k + 1)) time. The initial integer interval has k+1 candidates and each comparison halves it.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. A constant number of integer accumulators is retained.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/IntSquareRoot.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: The inclusive search interval contains the boundary between integers whose squares are at most k and those whose squares exceed k. A feasible middle discards itself and all smaller candidates by moving left past it; an infeasible middle moves right before it. At termination left is the first infeasible integer, so left-1 is the floor root.
walkthrough: For k=80, binary search eventually tests 8 and 9. Since 8²=64≤80 but 9²=81>80, return 8.
edgeCases: Perfect squares return their exact root.
Square candidates in long arithmetic to avoid overflow near int.MaxValue.
